corArgs API

The command line of every program of the stack, from one table: each option's name, short name, type, range, default, environment variable and help. corArgs parses the command line and the environment against it, refuses a value of the wrong type or out of range, and prints -u / -U from the same table - so the help cannot disagree with what is accepted.

Below: every header of corArgs at 44bbe9f6 - 18 headers, 36 entries, each with its declarations as written and its comment. Included as "corArgs/<header>".

CorArg

typedef struct CorArg
{
  const char*  longName;       // Long name of the option, e.g. --port
  const char*  shortName;      // MUST start with '-' or '+'
  CorArgType   type;           // type: bool, int, string, etc
  void*        valueP;         // points to where to store the value
  CorArgSort   sort;           // sort: optional, required, hidden
  void*        def;            // default value
  void*        min;            // lower limit
  void*        max;            // upper limit
  const char*  description;    // textual description for usage
} CorArg;

#define _vp (void*)

CorArgInfo.h

CorArgInfo

typedef struct CorArgInfo
{
  char*          longName;       // Long name of the option, e.g. --port
  char*          shortName;      // MUST start with '-' or '+'
  CorArgType     type;           // type: bool, int, string, etc
  void*          valueP;         // points to where to store the value
  CorArgSort     sort;           // sort: optional, required, hidden
  void*          def;            // default value
  void*          min;            // lower limit
  void*          max;            // upper limit
  char*          description;    // textual description for usage
  bool           secret;         // never shown - corArgsSecret()

  bool           builtin;
  bool           disabled;
  CorArgValueFrom  from;
  char           envVar[60];
} CorArgInfo;

CorArgsError.h

CORARGS_ERROR_PUSH

#define CORARGS_ERROR_PUSH(optionName, status, description)                                       \
do                                                                                              \
{                                                                                               \
  COR_LIB_E("CorArgs Error %s for option '%s': %s", corArgsStatus(status), optionName, description);  \
  corArgsErrorPush(__FILE__, __LINE__, __FUNCTION__, optionName, errno, status, description);     \
} while (0)

CorArgsError

typedef struct CorArgsError
{
  char*              fileName;
  int                lineNo;
  char*              funcName;
  char*              optionName;
  int                errNo;
  CorArgsStatus      status;
  char*              description;
  struct CorArgsError* next;
} CorArgsError;

corArgsErrorPush

push an error to the error stack

extern void corArgsErrorPush
(
  const char*  fileName,
  int          lineNo,
  const char*  funcName,
  const char*  optionName,
  int          errNo,
  CorArgsStatus  status,
  const char*  description

This is an internal function. It should be used *only* by the internal macro 'CORARGS_ERROR_PUSH'.

corArgsEnvError

the first value of the environment that was refused, the text that says so; corArgsParse

extern char          corArgsEnvError[1024];
extern CorArgsStatus corArgsEnvStatus;
extern bool          corArgsEnvReading;

says it after its -u/-U check, so a bad CORAINE_PORT does not keep the usage from being printed. corArgsEnvStatus: its status, CorArgsOk for none. corArgsEnvReading: the environment is being read - corArgsSay writes into corArgsEnvError instead of stdout

corArgsSecret.h

corArgsSecret

mark an option, by its long name, as one whose value is never shown: a password, a URI that

extern bool corArgsSecret(const char* longName);

may hold credentials. A tool listing the options (coraine's GET /admin/config) masks it.

Called after the option is declared (corArgsInit, or corArgsAdd for a plugin's).

@return false: no such option
